questions.text:
In designing a computer's cache system, the cache block (or cache line) size is an important
Parameter. Which one of the following statements is correct in this context?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Smaller blocks bring fewer neighbouring words, so spatial locality is used less.
- Smaller blocks mean more blocks [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] more tags overall, i.e. more tag overhead.
- On a miss only a small block is transferred, so miss penalty is lower [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.

Answer: A smaller block size incurs a lower cache miss penalty

options: A smaller block size implies better spatial locality
A smaller block size implies a smaller cache tag and hence lower cache tag overhead
A smaller block size implies a larger cache tag and hence lower cache hit time
A smaller block size incurs a lower cache miss penalty

questions.text:
A 4-way set-associative cache memory unit with a capacity of 16 KB is built using a block
size of 8 words. The word length is 32 bits. The size of the physical address space is 4 GB.
The number of bits for the TAG field is _____
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Block = 8 words [latex]\times[/latex] 4 B = 32 B [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] offset = 5 bits
- Blocks = 16 KB / 32 B = 512, sets = 512 / 4 = 128 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] index = 7 bits
- Address = 4 GB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 32 bits

TAG = 32 [latex]-[/latex] 7 [latex]-[/latex] 5 = 20 bits

Answer: 20

questions.text:
Consider two processors P1 and P2 executing the same instruction set. Assume that under
identical conditions, for the same input, a program running on P2 takes 25% less time but
incurs 20% more CPI (clock cycles per instruction) as compared to the program running on
P1. If the clock frequency of P1 is 1GHz, then the clock frequency of P2 (in GHz) is _________.
questions.solution:
Time = IC [latex]\times[/latex] CPI / f. With [latex]T_2=0.75T_1[/latex] and [latex]CPI_2=1.2\,CPI_1[/latex]:
[latex]0.75=\frac{1.2}{f_2/f_1}\Rightarrow f_2=\frac{1.2}{0.75}\times1=1.6[/latex] GHz

Answer: 1.6

questions.text:
An access sequence of cache block addresses is of length N and contains n unique block
addresses. The number of unique block addresses between two consecutive accesses to the
same block address is bounded above K. What is the miss ratio if the access sequence is
passed through a cache of associativity A[latex]\geq[/latex]k exercising least-recently-used replacement policy?
questions.solution:
Between two uses of the same block, at most k other blocks are used, and the cache holds A [latex]\ge[/latex] k blocks per set with LRU. So a block is never evicted before it is used again: only the first access to each of the n distinct blocks misses.

Miss ratio = n / N

Answer: n/N

questions.text:
Consider a 6-stage instruction pipeline, where all stages are perfectly balanced. Assume that
there is no cycle-time overhead of pipelining. When an application is executing on this 6-stage pipeline, the speedup achieved with respect to non-pipelined execution if 25% of the instructions incur 2 pipeline stall cycles is _________.
questions.solution:
Pipelined CPI = 1 + 0.25 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 1.5. A balanced 6-stage pipeline ideally gives speedup 6.

Speedup = 6 / 1.5 = 4

Answer: 4
